A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoTemp-o3 and contain the full main text and Appendices A–G. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of their equations, tables, figures, and case studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, grounding analyses, RL training dynamics, and model-output case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original benchmark results, ablations, training analyses, and case studies, including those in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same iterative localize–clip–answer procedure, final-two-turn SFT masking, and penalty-aware IoU reward. No algorithmic component or objective changes.

E1.justification: The training sources and evaluation coverage remain unchanged across long-video understanding, temporal grounding, and grounded QA. VideoTemp-Bench retains the same four duration groups and source datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables and appendix analyses, including Qwen2.5-VL-7B, VideoChat-R1-7B, Video-R1-7B, and the task-specific comparison methods.

E3.justification: Table 6 and Appendix B.2 retain the same configurations and evaluation procedures. Appendix B.1 newly specifies a separate 64-frame clip limit; v1 did not state a separate clip budget, so this is additional disclosure under D1 rather than an established change to the experiments.

E4.justification: The grounding-data, masking, and reward ablations are unchanged. The tool-use analyses, ground-truth-segment experiment, reward dynamics, and Appendix G case studies are also retained without changes.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, with no added or revised evaluation-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported scores, plotted findings, and case outputs match. For example, Table 1 retains the RL model's 64.5 VideoMME overall score and 43.0 LVBench score; appendix results are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The trajectory formulation, GRPO objective, and reward definitions in Equations 1–6 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified grounding and QA, on-demand cropping, iterative refinement, training strategies, and dataset construction.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reward hacking, grounding as a long-video bottleneck, and weaknesses in counting, OCR, and temporal reasoning remain unchanged. Appendices C–D retain the same mechanism explanations and qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 now distinguishes a 512-frame maximum for original videos from a 64-frame maximum for clips, where v1 gave only a general 512-frame limit. It also removes the NVIDIA H200 specification, retaining only eight GPUs. Other technical details and access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are unchanged. No cited works or substantive relationships to prior research are added, removed, or redefined.

P1.justification: v3 replaces placeholder correspondence details with named contacts, adds author-role markers, and lightly revises Appendix B.1. The section organization and scientific narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Author-block and project-link formatting change, producing limited text reflow on pages 1–4; Appendix B.1 also has different line wrapping. All figures and tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The explicit 64-frame clip limit in Appendix B.1 makes training inputs easier to reproduce, and actual correspondence details replace placeholders. Removing the H200 specification weakens hardware reporting, but the added sampling detail provides a modest net gain in practical clarity. The scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
